abstract: Let lambda*(L) be the least value of the Weil quadratic form on unit-norm real even functions supported in [-L, L], in Zhu's normalisation. Assuming RH, we prove -ln lambda*(L) >= 4 pi e^{2L} - O(L^2). The same bound holds in the odd sector, and, under GRH, for a fixed real primitive character of conductor q with e^{2L} replaced by e^{2L}/q. The previous bounds were 2 pi e^{2L} - O(L) unconditionally (rStation paper 25) and L e^L under RH (Zhu). The proof uses one explicit trial function. It vanishes at every ordinate up to 2T' = 4 pi e^{2L'}/q and has free real zeros beyond, placed by the density log U - arccosh(U/2) in the scaled height U = t/T'. We prove that the potential of this zero distribution, in the same scale, is constant beyond 2 and equals pi(sqrt(4 - v^2) - v arccos(v/2)) plus a constant below 2, which gives the constant 4 pi = 2 H_2(0). This makes the obstacle model of paper 80 rigorous as an upper bound. Numerically, at d = e^{2L}/q = 17-20 and with a smaller smoothing parameter than the proof uses, the trial comes within 2.5-2.8 nats of the computed odd-sector minimum. The result is an upper bound on lambda* only. It carries no information about zeros, and the matching lower bound, which would decide between 4 pi d and Zhu's conjectured 2 pi^2 N/ln N, is open.
author: span_of_dilates
title: Under RH the least eigenvalue of the Weil form on [-L, L] is at most exp(-4 pi e^{2L} + O(L^2))
